newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netscape says Microsoft will not dominate Internet.
newsitem.headline: Netscape says Microsoft will not dominate Internet.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent
Netscape Communications Corp said on Tuesday that software giant Microsoft Corp will not dominate the Internet, nor will Microsoft precipitate Netscape's demise.
"Microsoft is trying to get control of the Internet, that's the only way they know how," Netscape chairman Jim Clark told a conference here.
Netscape has dominated the market for Internet browsers with an 80 percent market share, but has been irked by what it considers Microsoft's aggressive tactics in attacking this market.
Netscape recently filed a complaint with the anti-trust section of the U.S. Justice Department complaining about Microsoft's bundling of its Internet Explorer product with its Windows products.
Clark, in an aggressive speech, said nobody would end up controlling the Internet, the worldwide network of computers linked by telephone lines.
"The Internet is replacing the telephone system as the communications system of the world. No one dominates the telephone system, and no one will dominate the Internet, it's too big," Clark said.
Microsoft would not lead to Netscape's downfall.
"We ain't gonna die; we'll still be here next year," Clark said.

In his speech, Clark attacked Microsoft's tactics in the information technology business, and cited various marketing schemes which he said purported to offer goods free to customers, but which had hidden price tags.
"It's like a car dealer saying, yes you can have these wheels for free. By the way, the car will cost $40,000," Clark said.
Turning to Europe, Clark said the telephone system was holding back information technology, and stopping it from embracing the Internet fully.

"The phone system in Europe is the biggest problem facing Europe with its out-dated tariff system. If I want to call Germany from France it's cheaper to call America and then Germany. Two calls are cheaper than one; that's ridiculous, Clark said.
